H4_System_Architecture.title: h4_Live: How it works
H4_System_Architecture.description: Welcome to h4_Live—a toolkit designed to make ComfyUI feel a bit more like a collaborative workspace. Instead of one giant file, we use a modular system. Every node is its own separate folder inside `/nodes/`. This makes it easy to add or remove features without breaking the whole thing. The 'Core' engine handles the behind-the-scenes logic while the nodes handle the actual art.
tips: You can delete any folder in /nodes/ to safely remove that node if you don't need it.
Adding a new folder in /nodes/ automatically syncs its code to the UI.
The /core/ folder is the main engine. Don't worry about touching it unless you're writing your own nodes.

KICK_THE_GRID.title: (>_<)!! — KICK THE GRID (UI Reset)
KICK_THE_GRID.description: Found in the top-right toolbar, the **KICK THE GRID** button is an emergency tool for when your UI gets stuck. If your nodes stop moving, your wires look 'frozen,' or you just can't click anything, this button refreshes the graph layout and logic without reloading your whole browser. It's a quick way to clean up visual glitches without losing your place in the queue.
KICK_THE_GRID.usage: Click the button if the UI feels slow or wires look messy. You'll see a quick Kirby-style face update as it works.

warning.title: Visual Themes
warning.content: If you are using custom themes that change how wires look (like making them look like pipes or circuit boards), a Grid Kick might not fix all visual glitches. You might still need a full browser refresh if the wires themselves look broken.

tips: Use this before refreshing the browser to try and keep your queued jobs running.
If nodes are trapped on top of each other, this can often shake them loose.
It's the first thing you should try if an H4 node isn't displaying its thumbnails correctly.

H4_ModelMerger.title: H4 Model Merger (The Lab)
H4_ModelMerger.description: This is a tool for blending different AI models together to create something unique. Instead of just picking one model, you can mix the strengths of several. You might take the realistic lighting from one and the character style from another. It gives you a lot of control over which parts of the models to mix, so you can avoid making a 'muddy' result. Just be careful with the sliders—sometimes mixing too much can lead to weird colors or glitchy images.
H4_ModelMerger.usage: Use this node to build your own custom 'Merged' models without needing extra tools. You can mix up to three models at a time and see a test image instantly so you know if the blend is working.

model_count.description: How many checkpoints are we smashing together? '2' is the standard (Base + Style). '3' is for when you're feeling greedy or trying to balance out two strong styles with a neutral base.

w_1 / w_2 / w_3.description: The 'Global Influence' for each model. This acts as a multiplier for everything underneath. If you set Model 2 to 0.5, even its strongest blocks will only contribute half their power to the final mix.

settings.description:
Flip this switch to unlock the **'Mad Science'** drawer. It reveals granular weight sliders for every single block of the UNet. 

 - **IN0-11**: The foundation. Affects composition, layout, and large shapes. 
 - **MID**: The core logic and coherence. 
 - **OUT0-11**: The finish. Affects textures, lighting, shading, and style. 

 If you leave this OFF, I just do a standard merge based on your Global Weights. But where's the fun in that?

memory_manager.description: Look, merging models takes VRAM. A lot of it. If you're rocking a 4090, you can leave this OFF. But for the rest of us mortals with <24GB VRAM, turn this ON. It implements my **Intelligent Memory Protocol**: loading models one by one, merging them, and flushing them from cache instantly. It's slower, but it stops your PC from crashing.

testing_mode.description: This just shows/hides the internal test generator parameters. Note: The node ALWAYS generates a test image (or latent) to show you the result. This toggle just lets you see the seed/steps knobs.

interpolation_mode.description:
The mathematical formula I use to blend the weights. 

 - **Weighted Average**: Standard base/ratio blend. 
 - **Symmetric Average**: My preferred mode for 3-model merges. It balances Model 1's base against the invaders. 
 - **Add Difference**: For 'Delta' merging (Checkpoint A + (Checkpoint B - Checkpoint C)).

decode_test_image.description: Listen, VAE decoding is heavy. If you're merging huge SDXL models and just want a quick check, turn this OFF. I'll give you a raw LATENT output instead. Saves VRAM, saves time. I'll show a blue placeholder image to remind you it's running 'Latent Only' mode.

test_width / test_height.description: The dimensions of the internal test generation. Default is 512 because it's fast, but for SDXL merges, you probably want 1024 or higher provided your GPU doesn't melt.

clip_source / vae_source.description: Select exactly which model provides the CLIP and VAE. Often, a 'Merged' CLIP is what you want, but sticking to Model 1's VAE ensures color consistency.

test_seed.description: (Testing Mode) Seed for the internal test generation.

test_prompt.description: (Testing Mode) Prompt for the test image.
test_prompt.example: masterpiece, best quality, a beautiful landscape

outputs.MODEL: The resulting frankenstein Model (UNet). Pipe this into your KSampler.
outputs.CLIP: The merged CLIP model. Don't forget this! Text encoding needs to match the UNet usually.
outputs.VAE: The VAE from the chosen model. Essential for decoding.
outputs.TEST_LATENT: The raw latent output of the internal test generation. Perfect for sending to a separate 'Save Latent' node or HiRes Fix.
outputs.TEST_IMAGE: The decoded image of the test generation. If 'decode_test_image' is OFF, this will be a blue square. Don't panic, it's a feature.

features.name: Smart Decode
features.description: I put some brains in the decoder. If your image is gargantuan (>1024px), I automatically switch to 'Tiled' mode to save memory. Small image? Standard fast decode.

features.name: FP32 Fallback
features.description: Ever get those dreaded black square outputs? Yeah, I hate them too. This node detects if the VAE crapped out (NaNs or zeros) and automatically retries the decode in full Float32 precision. It just works.

features.name: Architecture Safety
features.description: Trying to merge an SD1.5 model with an SDXL turbo model? That's illegal. And it creates garbage static. I check the architecture type before merging and scream at you in the console if they don't match.

tips: Use 'Symmetric Average' if you are merging 3 models and want Model 1's unique features to stand a fighting chance.
Unlock 'Settings' to experiment. Lower Input blocks usually affect composition/shapes. Higher Output blocks affect fine details/textures/lighting.
If you seek pure speed, turn 'decode_test_image' OFF and use the 'TEST_LATENT' output.

H4_Comparinator.title: H4 Comparinator (A/B Test)
H4_Comparinator.description: A tool for comparing two images side-by-side. It's useful for seeing exactly how a small change in your prompt or settings affects the final result. You can slide between images, zoom in to see fine details, and browse through your history to find that one generation you liked from ten minutes ago.
H4_Comparinator.usage: Drop this at the end of your workflow. It starts in a simple view, but you can toggle the 'Histories' button to see your past renders or 'Inspectinator' to zoom in on specific areas.

image_a.description: The 'Primary' or 'Before' image. Usually your latest generation (Live Slot).

image_b.description: The 'Secondary' or 'After' image. If empty, the node automatically pulls from the Vault history.

frozen_image.description: The 'Anchor'. Overrides Image B. Perfect for freezing a 'Gold Reference' you want to beat.

save_mode.description: Flip to **💾 SAVE** to commit your comparison captures to disk. In **PREVIEW** mode, images are temporary and will eventually vanish into the Ether.

features.name: Tri-State Selection Workflow
features.description:
Interact with the filmstrip history like a pro. 
 - **GREEN**: Primary reference (Selected). 
 - **RED**: Secondary reference (OtherB) for dual-histories comparison. 
 - **YELLOW**: Persistent Lock (Shift+Right Click). The image stays put even as you queue new jobs.

features.name: Sniper Scope Optics
features.description: High-performance slaving between the Navigator (left) and Magnifier (right). The reticle itself acts as a scope, displaying a magnified 'micro-preview' while you hunt for artifacts.

features.name: Histories Mode
features.description: An expanded 50/50 dual-pane mode. Compares your latest generation against your Green-selection AND your Green-selection against your Red-selection simultaneously. Total diagnostic coverage.

features.name: Telemetry Drawer
features.description: A slide-up panel that reveals the DNA of the selected image. It separates 'Prompt Specs' (Models, VAEs, CLIPs, LoRAs) from 'Generation Settings' (Seed, CFG, Denoise) for easy reading.

tips: Use the 'Blink' mode (Spacebar) for high-frequency difference detection between A and B.
Right-click the filmstrip to instantly clear all diagnostic selections and go back to lean mode.
The Sniper Scope background magnification is calculated at 1.5x of your magnifier zoom to provide the best 'hunting' experience.

H4_SmartSave.title: H4 SmartSave (The Vault — +ULTRA Edition)
H4_SmartSave.description:
Welcome to the ultimate forensic terminal. SmartSave is the definitive image archiving and interaction authority for ComfyUI. It's not just a file saver; it's a sentient metadata vault that records the exact DNA of your workflow. It features a high-performance filmstrip for historical traversal, a deep-zoom Lightbox for pixel inspection, and a multi-tiered diagnostic HUD that pulls every setting from your graph without you ever having to lift a finger (or a wire). 

 **⚠️ WORK IN PROGRESS**: We are currently hardening the thumbnail preloading engine. You may experience transient 'Ghost Frames' (desynced thumbnails) during intense GPU load. The core forensic data is always preserved; this is a purely visual artifact.
H4_SmartSave.usage: Drop this into your workflow to replace the standard 'Save Image'. Use the [H], [P], and [M] buttons to toggle the History Bar, the Workflow Parameter drawer, and the Metadata injection panel. It works best when you want to look at everything you've done today without drowning in PNG folders.

images.description: The art. The pixels. The soul. Everything you generate passes through here to be archived forever.

filename_prefix.description: Organization matters. Use slashes like `WAIFUS/V1` to create folders automatically. Supports date codes like `%date:yyyy-MM-dd%` to keep your renders perfectly indexed.

save_mode.description:
The traffic light for your hard drive. 
 **🟢 SAVE**: Commits to disk (Permanent). 
 **🟡 PREVIEW**: Just shows in the HUD (Temporary). Use Preview until you've nailed the prompt, then flip it to Save for the final result.

output_path.description: Optional: Write your images to a specific drive or a top-secret folder. I'll handle all the subfolder logic from there.

author.description: Burn your name into the PNG 'Author' tag. Claim your masterpiece.

model_name.description: The name of the checkpoint used. Essential for forensic backtracking months later.

comments.description: Personal diary notes saved in the image file. 'Lighting was good, hands need fix'. These are permanent.

custom_json.description: Weaponized metadata injection. Valid JSON here is embedded directly in the PNG header. Use it for tracking specific experiment IDs or custom parameter blocks.

features.name: Recursive Forensic Engine (v24.14.38)
features.description: The smartest part of the node. It autonomously crawls your workflow graph backwards recursively to find every single node connected to the image chain. It extracts their current state, widget values, and internal logic to populate the [P] Parameter drawer with zero-wire simplicity.

features.name: Tier-2 Insight Drawers
features.description: Deep-dive diagnostic HUD. Clicking any node card in the Parameters list slides out a secondary drawer containing the full internal state, specific IDs, and raw values for that particular node. Multi-tiered tactical inspection.

features.name: Viewport Sovereignty Protocol
features.description: The node intelligently synchronizes its DOM presence with your canvas view. Elements are purged from the document body if the node is off-screen or zoomed out past the 0.35x interactive floor, ensuring 100% ghost-free, high-performance canvas interaction.

features.name: Lightbox Traveler v3
features.description: Double-click any thumbnail to enter the Lightbox. Now features full keyboard navigation (Arrows), high-fidelity zoom up to 500%, and persistent index tracking so you can trawl through months of work in one sitting.

features.name: Shadow Banishment
features.description: Standard ComfyUI widgets are kept alive in the backend for prompt validation but are physically banished to -9999px in the UI. This grants the H4 Sovereign HUD absolute, unobstructed authority over the visual real estate.

features.name: History Filmstrip (Tactical Nav)
features.description: A high-performance horizontal gallery of your last generations. Use the bottom-left [H] button to toggle it. It's virtualized to handle hundreds of images without lagging your browser.

features.name: FIFO Digital Janitor
features.description: First-In-First-Out logic. I keep the last 25 images per prefix subfolder and automatically prune the oldest files, keeping your output directory clean and your storage happy.

features.name: Asset Synchronization (The RX)
features.description: Unified asset retrieval across Hover, Lightbox, and Canvas Background. By synchronizing every request with the preloader's unique timestamp hash, we ensure all elements hit the local browser cache, eliminating redundant backend traffic and ensuring instant tactile responsiveness.

tips: Organization is king: Use slashes in the prefix to group your work by project or version.
Use the JSON field to store structured data that you want to read back programmatically later.
If the UI feels 'ghostly' or misaligned, just refresh. The Sovereignty protocols are complex and love a fresh boot.
Double-click headers to collapse/expand drawers instantly for a cleaner look.

H4_Pythonipulator-inator.title: H4 Pythonipulator-inator (The image Kernel 🐍)
H4_Pythonipulator-inator.description: The ultimate image manipulation suite for h4_Live. It's a high-performance **Hybrid Kernel** that combines Pillow, OpenCV, and scikit-image into a single multi-threaded pipeline. Where standard nodes struggle with memory churn, the Kernel uses zero-copy transformations to apply complex filters (Chromatic Aberration, Glitch, Scanlines) in real-time. It's built for those who need surgical precision without the spaghetti wiring of 10 separate nodes.
H4_Pythonipulator-inator.usage: Connect an image and toggle the effect categories you want to use (Cyberpunk, Geometric, Color, Blur, etc.). Each category has a master 'Enabled' switch to keep things tidy. Use it to polish your results or as a creative tool to mess with your images in weird and wonderful ways.

image.description: The input image you want to manipulate.

operation_mode.description:
Choose the workflow state: 
 **🟢 Passthrough**: Just apply effects and send to the next node. 
 **💾 Save to Disk**: Apply effects and save files to your output folder. 
 **✨ Both**: Do everything.

cb_enabled (Cyberpunk).description: Unlock the futurist effects: Chromatic Aberration for that lens-distortion look, Glitch for digital artifacts, and Scanlines for that retro-CRT monitor vibe.

geo_enabled (Geometric).description: The canvas toolbox: Flip your image horizontally/vertically, rotate it by any angle, or resize it using specific scales or dimensions.

clr_enabled (Color).description: Standard processing: Brightness, Contrast, Saturation, and Sharpness. Also includes Invert (Negative) and Gamma correction for fixing washed-out lighting.

blur_enabled (Blur).description: Focus control: Gaussian and Box blurs for softness, or Median blur for that 'painted' look. Also features a dedicated Sharpen pass for crisp edges.

sty_enabled (Stylistic).description: Aesthetic filters: Pixelate your image for a retro look, or add a Vignette to darken the edges and draw the eye to the center.

noise_enabled (Noise).description: Grain control: Adds Gaussian noise to your image. Great for removing that 'too clean' AI look or matching film grain.

edge_enabled (Edge).description: Vision tools: Canny Edge detection. You can output just the lines (Standalone) or overlay the glowing edges on top of your original image (Overlay).

features.name: Surgical Drawer UI
features.description: The node stays compact by default. Toggling an 'Enabled' switch for a category like Color or Blur dynamically reveals all its associated sliders and knobs. It's professional tools without the clutter.

features.name: Tactical Save Engine
features.description: Integrated 'Save to Disk' logic. You can use this as your final node, specifying custom filenames and output folders directly on the face. It saves files incrementally with 'h4_' prefixes to prevent overwrites.

features.name: Inline Kernel Pipeline
features.description: Effects are processed sequentially in a sane order (Cyberpunk -> Geometric -> Color -> Blur -> etc.) so that resizing doesn't break your edge detection and sharpening happens after your color correction.

features.name: Dependency Sentinel
features.description: Smart enough to know what it needs. On first load, it scans your system for libraries like OpenCV or Scikit-Image. If they are missing, it initiates a 'Tactical Deployment' and installs them automatically for you.

tips: Use the 'Cyberpunk' scanlines at low values (0.1) to give images a subtle techy feel.
A small amount of 'Geometric' rotation (1-3 degrees) can sometimes fix perspective issues in AI generations.
Combine 'Edge' detection in 'Overlay' mode with 'Color' saturation for a stylized, comic-book look.
Use 'Pixelate' with 'Save to Disk' to quickly generate icons or low-res placeholders.

H4_TrafficCop.title: H4 Traffic Cop (Legacy Splitter)
H4_TrafficCop.description: Standard Logic Gates in ComfyUI are kinda... fragile. This node acts as a specific 'Start vs Loop' splitter. It takes one input and sends it to the 'Start' output on Run 0, and the 'Loop' output on Run 1+. It's a legacy version of the Router logic, useful for simpler setups.
H4_TrafficCop.usage: Use this if you want to fork a single input into two different processing chains based on whether it's the first run or a loop.

features.name: Safe Mode
features.description: It always sends data to prevent 'Missing Input' errors, but logically the workflow continues down the active path.

H4_TrafficMerge.title: H4 Traffic Merge (The Zipper)
H4_TrafficMerge.description: Okay, so you split your workflow into two paths. Now how do you bring them back together? With the Zipper. This node takes two inputs and intelligently selects the one that matches the current Loop Count phase. It also handles Denoise switching just like the Router.

restart_on_true.description: Reset signal. If True, resets count to 0.

loop_input.description: Input B (Loop 1+). WARNING: Use H4_ImageBuffer wireless mode! Wiring this directly often causes ComfyUI Cycle Errors.

H4_TrafficRouter.title: H4 Traffic Router (The Big Boss)
H4_TrafficRouter.description: This is the big daddy. It combines the Traffic Cop and Traffic Merge into one massive brain. It manages the 'Loop Count' of your workflow. Run 0 (Start)? It routes data from the 'First Run' input. Run 1+ (Loop)? It switches to the 'Loop Run' input. It completely automates multi-stage workflows.
H4_TrafficRouter.usage: The core of any 'Live Logic' or 'Feedback Loop' workflow. Connect your 'Load Image' to 'first_run_in' and your 'Refined Image' (from the end of the chain) to 'loop_run_in'.

first_denoise.description: Denoise strength for the very first generation (Run 0). Usually 1.0 (Full creativity).

loop_denoise.description: Denoise strength for subsequent loops (Run 1+). Usually lower (0.4-0.6) to refine the image without destroying it.

restart.description: Emergency switch. Toggle ON/OFF to reset the global loop counter back to 0. Useful if your loop gets stuck.

first_run_in.description: [OPTIONAL] The data source for the FIRST run (Loop 0). This is usually your 'Load Image' or empty latent.

loop_run_in.description: [OPTIONAL] The data source for LOOPS (Loop 1+). This comes from your feedback loop (e.g., the output of your sampler).

outputs.Context_Out: The active data stream (either First or Loop input, depending on the count).

features.name: State Memory
features.description: It remembers where it is. Run 0, Run 1, Run 50. It knows.

features.name: Auto-Denoise
features.description: Automatically switches the denoise value fed to the KSampler based on the loop stage.

H4_LoopIncrementer.title: H4 Loop Incrementer
H4_LoopIncrementer.description: The engine. This tiny node does one thing: It adds +1 to the global counter. But where you put it matters. Place it *after* your KSampler or Save Node. It ensures that the counter only goes up when a generation performs successfully.
H4_LoopIncrementer.usage: Connect your image output through this node. It passes the image through unchanged, but triggers the system to say 'Ok, Run 1 is done. Next is Run 2.'

wireless_reset.description: If ON, it listens for a mental signal from the Wireless Reset Button. No cables needed.

H4_WirelessResetButton.title: H4 Wireless Reset Button
H4_WirelessResetButton.description: It's a big red button. But virtual. And wireless. Sometimes your loop gets stuck or you just want to start fresh without reloading the workflow. Pressing (toggling) this sends a telepathic signal to the Loop Incrementer to reset the counter to 0.

H4_ImageBuffer.title: H4 Universal Buffer (The black Hole)
H4_ImageBuffer.description: Loops in ComfyUI are hard because of 'execution order'. The graph wants to move forward, not backward. The Image Buffer cheats. It creates a pocket dimension (global variable) where it stores the image from the end of the loop. Then, the Traffic Router can teleport that image back to the start for the next run. It eliminates the dreaded '1-Cycle Lag' where your loop is always using old data.
H4_ImageBuffer.usage: Put this at the VERY END of your loop chain. It catches the result and holds it for the Router.

image_in.description: Whatever you want to send back to the start. Image, Latent, Text... it takes it all.

features.name: Wireless Transmit
features.description: It beams the data to the Traffic Router without a physical wire. Prevents 'Cycle Detected' graph errors.

H4_StateMonitor.title: H4 State Monitor
H4_StateMonitor.description: Lost? Confused? Don't know if you're on Run 5 or Run 500? The State Monitor simply displays the current Loop Count as an integer. Wire it up to a display text node to keep track of your sanity.

Any_In.description: [Optional] Connect an output here to force execution order (daisy-chaining). The monitor will wait for this input before updating.

outputs.loop_count_number: The number. The count. The truth.

H4_ContextHub.title: H4 Context Hub (The Mothership)
H4_ContextHub.description: Spaghetti wires are the enemy of creativity. The Context Hub is your cable management solution. It takes up to 10 different types of inputs (Model, VAE, CLIP, Positive, Negative, Latent, Images, Masks...) and bundles them into a SINGLE distinct connection called 'H4_PIPE'. You can run this single purple wire across your entire graph.
H4_ContextHub.usage: Place this at the start of your workflow. Plug everything in. Then just run one wire to where you're going. You can even chain them by connecting an existing pipe to 'base_pipe'.

base_pipe.description: [Optional] Extend an existing pipe. If connected, we copy everything from it first, then overwrite with new inputs.

any_A.description: Wildcard Slot A. Put anything here.

any_B.description: Wildcard Slot B. Put anything here.

H4_ContextUnpack.title: H4 Context Unpack (The Receiver)
H4_ContextUnpack.description: The Receiver. It takes the single 'H4_PIPE' connection from the Mothership (Hub) and explodes it back out into its 10 individual components. Place this near your KSampler or Detailer nodes to get access to the models/conditions you bundled up earlier.

h4_pipe.description: The Purple Wire. Connect this to the Hub's output.

H4_LatentSelector.title: H4 Latent Selector (The Canvas)
H4_LatentSelector.description:
Don't guess resolutions. This node provides safe, trained aspect ratios for every major model (SD1.5, SDXL, Flux, and Wan/Z-Image video). It outputs a compliant empty latent and the width/height integers. 

 **Wan/Z-Image Support:** selects 720p/1080p equivalent resolutions.
H4_LatentSelector.usage: Pick a model type. Pick a shape. Connect to KSampler or VAE Encode.

base_model.description:
Which base architecture? 
 **SD1.5**: 512px base. 
 **SDXL**: 1024px base. 
 **Flux**: 1024px flexible. 
 **Wan/Z-Image**: 1280x720 base (Video).

aspect_ratio.description:
The shape. 16:9 for movies, 9:16 for TikTok, 1:1 for squares. 
 'Custom Dimensions' unlocks the sliders below.

batch_size.description: How many empty images to create.

H4_UniversalLoader.title: H4 Universal Loader (The Source)
H4_UniversalLoader.description:
The One Loader to Rule Them All. It handles standard Checkpoints (.safetensors) AND separated Diffusers components (UNET/CLIP/VAE). 

 **Features:** 
 - **Smart Validaton**: Detects if you mix SDXL limits with T5 encoders (crash prevention). 
 - **GGUF Support**: Auto-delegates to ComfyUI-GGUF input (if installed) for quantized models. 
 - **Wan Support**: Native detection and loading for Wan 2.1 video models (including GGUF).
H4_UniversalLoader.usage: Select 'Checkpoint' for normal use. Select 'Diffusers' for advanced mixing.

load_mode.description: Switch between standard files and component mixing.

unet_name.description: (Diffusers Mode) The UNET (diffusion model). Supports .safetensors and .gguf.

vae_name.description: (Diffusers Mode) The VAE. 'Baked / None' uses the one inside the checkpoint if available.

clip_name.description: Select the text encoder. If you are using a GGUF model, you might need a matching GGUF clip file. Otherwise, standard SDXL/SD1.5 clips work fine.

H4_ModelSave.title: H4 Model Save (The Vault)
H4_ModelSave.description: Saves your creation properly. Supports standard floating point formats (FP16, BF16, FP32) and the new Float8 formats (e4m3fn) if your torch version supports it. Features 'Nuclear RAM Saver' which writes the file iteratively to disk, preventing memory crashes when saving massive 10GB+ files.
H4_ModelSave.usage: Connect Model/CLIP/VAE. Pick a filename. Save.

save_dtype.description: Precision. 'float16' is standard. 'float8' is for future-proof shrinking.

save_meta.description: Embeds the prompt/workflow into the header.

H4_PixelPress.title: H4 Pixel Press (Sharpener)
H4_PixelPress.description: A tool for making your images look sharper and more vibrant. It works by upscaling the image, applying some lighting and color fixes (HDR), and then squishing it back down to create a 'denser', clearer look. It's great for removing that slightly blurry or 'soft' look that AI images sometimes have.
H4_PixelPress.usage: Connect your image, pick an upscale amount (like 2x), and enable HDR if you want more pop in the lighting.

supersample_scale.description: How much to upscale before squishing back down. 2x is standard. 4x is eager.

sharpness.description: Post-downscale sharpening. 0.3 is crisp. 1.0 is crunchy.

tiled_processing.description: Process in chunks to save VRAM. Crucial for 4x mode.

hdr_intensity.description: Global strength of the HDR effect.

enhance_color.description: Boosts color saturation slightly. Makes it pop.

upscale_model.description: Optional: Connect a model to use for the initial upscale. If empty, uses Lanczos.

tile_size.description: Tile size for processing to save VRAM. Lower if you OOM.

H4_Mutate.title: H4 Mutate (The Finisher)
H4_Mutate.description: A finishing tool for your images. It lets you add things like color grading, film grain, or sharpening to your final render. You can toggle on only the parts you need, like taking the style from one photo and applying it to your image, or just giving it a cinematic look with a film preset.
H4_Mutate.usage: Drop this right before you save your image. Use the toggles to open the different sections (Color, Style, Film, etc.) and adjust the sliders to taste.

enable_* toggles.description: There are 7 of these. They control the drawers. If you want to color grade, flip 'enable_color' to ON, and the color sliders will magically appear. Keep the node small by only turning on what you need.

pipeline_order.description: The sequence matters. Do you upscale *before* adding film grain, or *after*? 'default' does everything in a sane order. 'custom' lets you assign exact priority numbers to each effect.

hue_shift / saturation / gamma.description: (Color Section) The holy trinity of color correction. Gamma brightens midtones without blowing out your highlights.

scale_factor.description: (Upscale Section) 2.0 doubles the size. 0.5 shrinks it down.

style_method.description: (Style Section) How we steal the look. 'adain' and 'wct' use neural VGG networks for deep texture cloning. 'reinhard_color' is stupid fast but only steals the color palette.

style_image_1...4.description: (Dynamic Sockets) Plug a style reference image here. Once you plug one in, the next socket appears. Mutate can blend up to 4 styles together.

film_preset.description: (Film Section) 11 classic film stocks. Try CineStill 800T for cyberpunk vibes, or Velvia 50 for nuclear landscape colors.

mask.description: Want to only mutate the background? Plug a mask in here. Use 'mask_feather' to blur the edges so it blends seamlessly.

features.name: Dynamic Drawers
features.description: The node expands and contracts based on your toggles to save canvas space.

features.name: Neural Style Transfer
features.description: Includes genuine AdaIN and WCT style transfer engines running directly on pixels, without needing to loop back through a diffusion model.

features.name: Fallback Safety
features.description: If you feed it an impossible task and run out of VRAM, it catches the error and safely passes your original image through instead of crashing your render.

tips: Use 'mask' with a subtle 'mask_feather' to color grade just the subject or just the background.
If using 'wct' style transfer, keep your scale factor at 1.0 until you find the look you want, as it takes some compute.

H4_VisualTokenizer.title: H4 Visual Tokenizer (The Mind)
H4_VisualTokenizer.description: Visualize exactly how your prompt is broken down into tokens and weighted by the CLIP model. Helps debug why 'cat' is being ignored.
H4_VisualTokenizer.usage: Connect CLIP and write Text. Run. See visualization in the node.

clip.description: Connect your CLIP model here so the node knows which dictionary to use for the word-to-math conversion.

text.description: The prompt you want to analyze. Type your full prompt or wire it from a text node to see how it's broken down.

H4_MissionControl.title: H4 Mission Control (The Flight Deck)
H4_MissionControl.description:
This is the brain of your loop. While the Traffic Router handles the plumbing, Mission Control handles the administrative state. It increments the global Loop Counter, listens for Wireless Reset signals, and provides a central dashboard for your loop's status. It also acts as a pass-through for scheduler signals. 

 Think of it as the conductor of the orchestra. Without it, the violinists (your schedulers) don't know when to start playing.
H4_MissionControl.usage: Use this as the start of your 'Control Stack'. Set it to 'Active' to drive the loop. Set to 'Passive' if you just want to watch.

mode.description:
The Master Switch. 

 **Active (Master Base)**: This node is the Boss. It increments the Global Loop Counter every time it runs. Only ONE node in your entire workflow should be Active. 

 **Passive**: This node is a spectator. It reads the current loop count but does not touch it.

wireless_reset.description: ON = Check orbit storage for reset signal (Red Button). Only works in Active Mode.

debug_mode.description: Nuclear Logging. Turn this on if you want your console to scream values at you.

scheduler_val.description: Input for a Float Signal (from H4_LinearScheduler). Passes through.

scheduler_seed.description: Input for a Seed Signal (from H4_SeedGenerator). Passes through.

trigger_in.description: Daisy chain trigger. Connect anything here just to force execution order.

outputs.Dashboard_UI: Connect this to a Text Display node to see a live report of Run Count, Seed, and Scheduler values.

H4_LinearScheduler.title: H4 Linear Scheduler (The Ramp)
H4_LinearScheduler.description:
A mathematical ramp generator. It calculates a float value based on the current Loop Count progress. Want your Denoise to start at 1.0 and fade down to 0.1 over 10 loops? This does that math for you. 

 Formula: `Start + (End - Start) * (CurrentLoop / MaxLoops)`.
H4_LinearScheduler.usage: Connect the output to a 'Float' input on a KSampler or to 'scheduler_val' on Mission Control.

start_val.description: The value you want to start with on Run 0. For example, if you want high denoise at first, set this to 1.0.

end_val.description: The target value you want to reach by the end of your loop. For example, 0.2 for a sharp final image.

max_loops.description: How many runs it should take to move from the start value to the end value. If your loop goes longer than this, the value stays at the end point.

H4_SeedGenerator.title: H4 Seed Generator (Entropy Control)
H4_SeedGenerator.description:
Randomness is a tool, not a master. This node gives you precise control over your seeds during a loop. 

 Modes: 
 - **Fixed**: Always outputs the same seed. Good for testing logic changes. 
 - **Incremental**: Outputs (Start_Seed + Loop_Count). Deterministic but changing. Good for sweeps. 
 - **Random**: Pure chaos. New seed every time.
H4_SeedGenerator.usage: Connect this to the 'scheduler_seed' input of Mission Control.

start_seed.description: Your starting number. If you're using Incremental mode, this is where the counting begins.

mode.description:
Decide how the numbers change each run. 

 **Incremental**: Adds the current run number to the start seed. 
 **Fixed**: Never changes. 
 **Random**: Picks a completely new number every time.

H4_DebugErrorGenerator.title: H4 Debug Error Generator (The Self-Destruct)
H4_DebugErrorGenerator.description: DO NOT TOUCH THIS. Unless you are developing error handling logic. This node exists solely to crash the system intentionally so we can test if the 'Death Modal' popup works correctly. If you put this in your workflow and set it to 'Critical', you deserve what happens. It tests sanitization, traceback hiding, and GitHub search links.

error_type.description:
Choose your poison. 
 'minor': ValueError. 
 'warning': RuntimeError with fake sensitive data. 
 'critical': Nested Exception crash.

trigger.description: Pull the pin. If True, it crashes immediately.

outputs.status: You won't see this because it crashed.

H4_Discombobulator.title: The Discombobulator
H4_Discombobulator.description: (b'.')b  t('.'t) ... A harmless easter egg node. It intercepts ComfyUI input/queue notifications and translates them into Leet Speak, Binary, or Glitch text in the side panel. It does absolutely nothing to your images. It just makes the UI feel like a hacker movie.

discombobulation_choice.description: Choose the dialect (1337, Binary, B64, Void).

H4_Gridinator.title: H4 Gridinator (The Grid Maker)
H4_Gridinator.description: A node for creating grids of images to compare different settings. You can test multiple models, prompts, or things like 'Steps' and 'CFG' all at once. It's designed to be efficient, so it tries to group tasks together to save time and memory. It's the best way to see a big range of options without rendering them one-by-one manually.
H4_Gridinator.usage: Connect your checkpoint and set what you want to test on the X, Y, and Z axes. It will generate a large sheet showing all the variations.

image_upload.description: CRITICAL FOR IMG2IMG. Upload your source image here. If I see an image, I automatically enter Img2img mode. If empty, I default to Txt2Img. Supported: .jpg, .png, .webp.

base_model.description: THE BRAIN: Your primary Checkpoint. For grids comparing OTHER models, this acts as the default if an axis value is missing.

base_model_fuzzy.description: FUZZY HUNTER: Can't find your model? Type a piece of the name here (e.g., 'juggernaut'). I'll scan your folders and find the best match. This OVERRIDES the dropdown.

grid_x/y/z_mode.description:
Choose your dimension! 

 - **Model**: Swap checkpoints. 
 - **LoRA**: Test strengths or different LoRAs. 
 - **Prompt**: Every cell gets a unique prompt. Splits by **NEWLINES**. 
 - **Multi-Prompt**: The **{Brace}** system. See features below! 
 - **Prompt Stutter**: Randomizes your prompt variations. 
 - **CFG/Steps/Denoise**: Standard setting sweeps.

stutter_mode.description:
PROMPT AUTOMATION. 

 - **Permutations**: Splits {red|blue} into multiple cells. 
 - **Emphasis**: Expands [dog*3] into 'dog dog dog'.

sliding_scale_enable.description: AUTO-GENERATOR. Turn this ON to automatically generate a linear range between Min and Max values for Steps or Denoise. No more typing '0.1, 0.2, 0.3...'

features.name: The {Brace} System (Multi-Prompt)
features.description:
This is the king of prompt testing. When using 'Multi-Prompt' mode, I look for content inside `{}` curly braces. This allows you to use commas naturally inside your tags without breaking the grid. I also ignore anything *between* the braces (dots, slashes, notes), giving you a clean visual layout.

 **Example 1**: `{1girl, beach}` / `{1girl, forest}`
 **Example 2**: `{blue eyes}.{red eyes}.{green eyes}`
features.example: Use this to test wildly different concepts on one axis.

features.name: VRAM Optimization Loop
features.description: I don't just run images in order (0,0,0 -> 0,0,1). I pre-calculate every task and group them by Model and LoRA. I'll load Model A, run all associated cells, then swap once to Model B. This saves massive amounts of time and VRAM fragmentation.

features.name: Dynamic Label Sizing
features.description: I measure the text bounds of your labels and automatically expand the grid margins to fit. Whether your prompt is 'Cat' or 'A hyper-detailed masterpiece of a futuristic cat in space', the label will never be cut off.

features.name: SDXL Auto-Safety
features.description: I automatically detect if you are using SDXL models and encourage 1024x1024 resolutions to prevent those weird 'low-res' artifacting issues. I'll even warn you if your dimensions are not multiples of 8.

tips: Use the 'Fuzzy Hunter' for models if you have a massive library. It's much faster than scrolling.
For Multi-Prompt mode, put your prompts in braces `{prompt}` to keep things tidy.
Combine 'Linear Scheduler' (Sliding Scale) on one axis with 'Models' on another to find the 'Sweet Spot' for a new checkpoint.

H4_DataStream.title: H4 DataStream (The Feed)
H4_DataStream.description: Batch processing made simple. This node loads images (or video frames) from a local folder one by one. But the killer feature is 'Auto-Queue'. Turn it on, queue IT ONCE, and it will automatically re-queue itself until the entire folder is processed. It handles video files too (requires OpenCV). It also creates intelligent thumbnails for the UI.
H4_DataStream.usage: Point it at a folder. Set Index to 0. Auto-Queue = True. Queue Prompt.

folder_path.description: Absolute path to your images/video. Windows example: C:\My_Dataset. Linux: /home/user/dataset.

current_index.description: The cursor. Points to the current image number (0-indexed). The node auto-increments this internally during Auto-Queue, but you can manually set it to skip ahead.

auto_queue_remaining.description: The infinite loop switch. If ON, the node will check if there are more images. If yes, it triggers a new queue instantly. Consumes the folder until empty.

outputs.current_index: The number of the current frame.
outputs.total_count: Total files in the folder (or frames in video).
outputs.is_last: Boolean. True if this is the final image.

H4_AxisDriver.title: H4 Axis Driver (Grid Logic)
H4_AxisDriver.description: This is a companion node for the Gridinator. It helps set up the different 'axes' for your grid—like testing several models on the X-axis and different CFG values on the Y-axis. It creates a structured set of instructions that the Gridinator uses to render the right images in the right order. It's usually controlled by high-level menu settings, but you can also see the summary of your grid right on the node face.
H4_AxisDriver.usage: Connect the axis outputs to the Gridinator. Use the custom menu to pick what you want to test, and watch the summary text to make sure your grid isn't too large to finish.

config.description: The technical instructions for the grid. This is usually handled automatically, but it describes which values are being tested on each axis.

outputs.axis_z: Instructions for the depth (Z) axis (used for 3D grids).
outputs.legacy_summary: A simple text list showing exactly what your grid will test.

H4_DisplayAny.title: H4 Display Any (Universal Monitor)
H4_DisplayAny.description:
Stop guessing what your data looks like. This node accepts ANY input type (Image, Latent, String, List, Dict, Tensor) and visualizes it. If you plug in an image, you get a thumbnail. If you plug in a Latent, you get shape info. If you plug in a dictionary, you get JSON. 

 **Dynamic Slots**: Connect an input to 'source_1', and 'source_2' will magically appear. Connect that, and 'source_3' appears. You can monitor up to infinity (or until your screen runs out of space).
H4_DisplayAny.usage: Plug stuff in. Read the output.

source_1.description: The first input slot. Connect anything here. More slots will spawn automatically.

H4_DocuScribe.title: H4 DocuScribe (The Stenographer)
H4_DocuScribe.description: Workflows get complicated. Remembering what settings you used for that one node 50 blocks back is impossible. DocuScribe fixes this. Connect any nodes you want directly to it, and it will crawl the graph backwards, extracting every setting, class name, and value, and compile them into a neat Markdown report saved to your output folder.
H4_DocuScribe.usage: Connect the nodes you want to document to 'source_1', 'source_2', etc. Run the workflow. Check your output folder.

source_1.description: The first node to document. More slots will appear automatically.

H4_FaceForge.title: H4 FaceForge (Face Swapper)
H4_FaceForge.description: A high-quality tool for swapping faces in your images. It doesn't just paste one face over another; it has options to clean up the details and make sure the skin textures blend naturally. It can also help keep faces from overlapping hair or hands using 'occlusion' filters.
H4_FaceForge.usage: Connect an image and a reference face. You can use the buttons to turn on restoration (to fix blur) or upscaling (to make it sharp).

input_image.description: The target image to operate on.

swap_enabled.description: The main switch. Turn this ON to swap faces. Turn OFF if you just want to use Restore or Upscale without changing identities.

swap_model.description: The brain that performs the swap. 'inswapper_128' is the standard one everyone uses. 'hyperswap' models are experimental.

target_face_index.description:
Which face to replace? 
 0 = The first face found. 
 1 = The second face. 
 0,2 = Swap the 1st and 3rd face. 
 -1 (if supported) = All faces.

source_face_index.description: Which face from the SOURCE image to use? Usually 0. If your source image has 5 people, pick the one you want to steal.

face_selection_mode.description:
How do we count faces? 
 **large-small**: Biggest face is #0. (Recommended) 
 **left-right**: Reading order. 
 **center**: Middle outward.

restore_enabled.description: Fixes blurry or pixelated faces. Great for low-res images or after a swap (swaps are 128px, they NEED this).

restore_model.description:
Choose the repair tool. 
 **GFPGAN**: Good general purpose. 
 **CodeFormer**: Stronger, but can change the identity slightly.

restore_visibility.description:
How strong is the repair? 
 1.0 = Full Model. 
 0.5 = 50% Mix with original (good for keeping texture).

codeformer_weight.description:
(CodeFormer Only) Balance between Quality (0.0) and Identity (1.0). 
 0.5 is a safe bet.

boost_enabled.description: **Experimental**: Enhances the face *during* the swap process, not just after. Slower, but can be sharper.

upscale_enabled.description: Make the image larger and crisper. Runs LAST.

upscale_model.description: The scaling engine. 'UltraSharp' is great for photos. 'R-ESRGAN' is standard.

upscale_face_only.description:
ON = Only sharpen the face (Fast). 
 OFF = Sharpen the whole image (Slower, but uniform).

occlusion_enabled.description:
**Smart Masking**. 
 Prevents the face from covering hair/hands/objects. 
 ⚠️ **WARNING**: Creates a SAM (Segment Anything) model which uses lots of VRAM. Don't use on 4GB cards.

preserve_glasses.description: (With Occlusion) Try to keep the original glasses on the face. Face Swappers are bad at glasses.

preserve_hair.description: (With Occlusion) Try to keep hair strands from being covered by the new face.

source_image.description: The face donor. (Optional if Face Model is connected).

face_model.description: A pre-compiled face embedding (Optional if Source Image is connected).

sam_model.description: The SAM model for occlusion. 'vit_b' is balanced.

H4_IdentityEngine.title: H4 Identity Engine (The Persona Engine)
H4_IdentityEngine.description: A tool designed for creating consistent characters across multiple images. It combines loading, prompting, and face swapping into one node so you can define a character's 'DNA' (their fixed appearance) and then just tell them what to do in each scene.
H4_IdentityEngine.usage: Load a saved character or connect a face photo. You can type your character's traits in the DNA box and their current action in the scene box.

preset.description: Load a saved character config (DNA + Face Model).

positive_dna.description: Permanent traits (e.g. 'blonde, scar on left cheek'). These are merged with your scene prompt every time.

positive.description: Scene Prompt: What they are doing right now.

vae_name.description: Color correction. 'Baked' means use what's inside the Checkpoint.

clip_name.description: Text Interpreter. 'Use Checkpoint' is usually best.

seed.description: The magic number definition. Same Seed + Same Settings = Same Image.

steps.description: How many times to polish the image. 20-30 is standard.

cfg.description: Creativity Scale. Low (5-7) = Creative. High (8-12) = Strict.

sampler_name.description: The drawing method. 'euler' is fast, 'dpmpp_2m' is detailed.

scheduler.description: How noise is removed. 'normal' or 'karras' work well.

denoise.description: Img2Img Only: How much to change the original? 1.0 = New Image, 0.4 = Minor Edits.

negative.description: What do you NOT want? (e.g. 'blurry, ugly, bad hands')

batch_size.description: How many images to create at once.

swap_enabled.description: Turn ON to enable face swapping.

face_similarity.description: How strictly to copy the face features. Higher = More likeness, but maybe weird.

H4_FaceDetailer.title: H4 Face Detailer (The Texture Fixer)
H4_FaceDetailer.description: This node is for fixing faces that look too smooth or blurry after a swap. It zooms in on the face, adds realistic details like skin pores or wrinkles, and then blends it back in. It helps make sure characters look high-resolution even in large 4K renders.

guide_size.description: Resolution to process the face crop at. 512 is standard. Higher = More Detail but slower.

denoise.description:
Texture hallucination strength. 
 0.2 = Just Pores. 
 0.5 = Plastic Surgery (Changes structure). 
 Keep it low (0.25 - 0.35).

force_inpaint.description: If True, uses inpainting logic for better blending.

model.description: The Model/LoRA stack used to generate the details.

vae.description: VAE for encoding/decoding the face crop.

guide_size_for.description: Reference size for the bounding box or the actual crop? Usually BBox is safer.

steps.description: Sampler steps for the detail pass.

positive.description: Prompts to guide the detailing. Keep it simple.

feather_mask.description: Softness of the paste edge in pixels.

outputs.face_crop: A crop of the face (for debugging/preview).

H4_BuildFaceModel.title: H4 Build Face Model (The Compiler)
H4_BuildFaceModel.description: Don't rely on a single photo for face swaps. This node takes a batch of images (or a folder path), extracts the face embeddings from ALL of them, and mathematically averages them into a 'Super Face'. This produces much higher resemblance and stability than a single reference image.
H4_BuildFaceModel.usage: Connect a batch of images (Load Image Batch) OR paste a folder path.

compute_method.description:
How do we blend the faces? 
 **Mean**: Average. Best for general use. 
 **Median**: Removes outliers (weird angles). 
 **Mode**: Centroid clustering.

folder_path.description: Path to a folder of images. Scans recursively.

det_size.description: Scan resolution. 640x640 finds small faces better. 320x320 is faster.

H4_SaveFaceModel.title: H4 Save Face Model
H4_SaveFaceModel.description: Saves your built Face Model to a .safetensors file. You can then load this file in FaceForge or IdentityEngine without needing to load the source images again.

filename.description: Name of the file. Don't add extension.

overwrite.description: Allow overwriting if the file already exists? Be careful.

outputs.SAVED_PATH: Absolute path to the saved file.

H4_DualCLIPTextEncode.title: H4 Dual CLIP Encode
H4_DualCLIPTextEncode.description: A utility that outputs BOTH the Conditioning (for the Sampler) and the raw String (for the Identity Engine's text input). Solves the spaghetti wiring problem.

H4_NodeTranslator.title: H4 Node Translator
H4_NodeTranslator.description: A utility that helps translate the names and labels of other nodes into different languages. It doesn't change how the nodes work, it just changes what you see on the screen. It's helpful if you prefer working in your native language instead of English.
H4_NodeTranslator.usage: Add this node to your workspace, set it to 'Active', and pick your language. It will automatically translate tags and labels across your whole canvas.

language.description: Choose your tongue. Supported: English, French (vrai), Spanish (cierto), Mandarin (true), German (echt).

mode.description:
**Active**: I'll translate everything. 
 **Disabled**: I'll step back and let the default English UI take over.

features.name: Case-Insensitive Mapping
features.description: My dictionary is smart. Whether a developer wrote 'Prompt', 'prompt', or 'PROMPT', I'll find it and translate it consistently.

features.name: Global Monospace Styling
features.description: I force a clean, technical monospace font across the UI when active. It makes everything easier to read and gives it that professional dev-tool look.

tips: If some nodes aren't translating, they might be using non-standard DOM structures. I'm always learning!
You only need one Translator node per workflow. It affects the entire canvas.

H4_Varianator.title: H4 Varianator (The Riff)
H4_Varianator.description: A dedicated variation engine. Takes a latent and produces N variations ('Riffs') on it. Perfect for exploring different seeds or slight denoise changes.
H4_Varianator.usage: Connect a Latent. Set Count. Queue.

variation_profile.description:
How different should they be? 
 **Minimal**: Subtle tweaks. 
 **Moderate**: Noticeable changes. 
 **Major**: Significant alterations.

seed_mode.description:
Control the randomness. 
 **Fixed**: Same variations every time. 
 **Increment**: Seed +1 for each variation. 
 **Random**: Total chaos.

base_seed.description: The starting point for the random number generator.

denoise.description: Strength of the variation. 1.0 = New Image.

H4_NoteInjector.title: H4 Note Injector
H4_NoteInjector.description: Adds a stylish title bar to your image. Great for labeling comparisons or adding context to a generation.

image.description: The image you want to write on. This is where the text bar will be added.

title_text.description: The main, large text you want to display on the bar.

bar_height.description: How thick the color bar should be in pixels. You might need to increase this if your font is very large.

position.description: Choose whether you want the text at the top or the bottom of the image.

font_size_title.description: How large the main title text should be.

font_size_sub.description: How large the smaller subtitle text should be.

text_color.description: The color of the text. Use a hex code like #FFFFFF for white or #000000 for black.

bar_color.description: The color of the background bar. Use a hex code like #000000 for a classic black bar.

subtitle_text.description: Extra info to show in smaller text, like the model name or the seed used.

H4_SmartConsole.title: H4 Smart Console (The Debugger)
H4_SmartConsole.description: The Inline Debugger. Displays data details in the console AND on the node itself. Useful for inspecting Tensors, Latents, or finding out what that 'Any' output actually contains.

+ULTRA.description: Turn this on for a much more detailed view. It will show hidden data, internal math, and technical stats that normal mode skips.

Anything In.description: The data you want to inspect. You can plug in images, text, models, or latents.

H4_PixelVisualizer.title: H4 Pixel Visualizer (The Diff)
H4_PixelVisualizer.description: Visualizes pixel-level differences between two images. Essential for testing if two latent processes produced identical results or checking compression artifacts.

image_a.description: The first image for the comparison.

image_b.description: The second image. We'll show you exactly how this one is different from the first one.

heatmap_scale.description: How much to 'glow' the differences. If you can't see anything, try increasing this to 10.0 or 20.0 to see microscopic pixel shifts.

H4_SeedSequencer.title: H4 Seed Sequencer (Controlled Chaos)
H4_SeedSequencer.description: A smarter, state-aware seed generator that remembers what it did last time. Unlike the basic Seed Generator which relies on the global loop count, the Sequencer maintains its own internal counter. This makes it perfect for workflows where you want the seed to advance independently of your loop logic. It also has a killer feature: Random Digits control. Instead of getting astronomically long random seeds like '352859205820582', you can tell it 'give me a 4-digit random seed' and get something clean like '9352' that's actually readable and typeable.
H4_SeedSequencer.usage: Set your starting seed, choose a mode (Fixed, Increment, or Random), and enable Auto-Advance if you want the seed to change between runs. For Random mode, set the digit count to control how long the random seed is.

seed.description: The starting number (your Base Anchor). In Fixed mode, this is always returned. In Increment mode, this is where counting starts. In Random mode, this is used as an initial value until the randomizer takes over.

mode.description: Fixed = Same seed every single time. Boring but reproducible. Increment = Adds the step value each run (e.g., Run1=100, Run2=101, Run3=102). Random = Pure chaos. New random seed every time, constrained by your digit setting.

increment_step.description: How much to add each run when in Increment mode. Set to 1 for sequential seeds, 10 for bigger jumps, or 1000 if you want to explore widely separated seed spaces.

auto_advance.description: If ON, the Sequencer remembers the seed for next time and advances automatically. If OFF, it acts like a one-shot and always returns the same calculated value.

random_digits.description: For Random Mode only: How many digits should the random seed be? Set to 4 for seeds like 1000-9999. Set to 10 for seeds like 1000000000-9999999999. Lower digits = easier to read and share.

outputs.seed: The generated seed integer. Wire this to your sampler's seed input.

tips: Use Increment mode with Auto-Advance ON for deterministic animation sequences—each frame gets a predictable, sequential seed.
Random mode with 4-digit seeds is perfect for quick exploration sessions where you want readable, shareable results.
If you manually change the seed widget while in Random mode, the Sequencer treats it as a 'manual override' and adopts your new value.

H4_Oxidine.title: H4 Oxidine (The Bundle)
H4_Oxidine.description: Oxidine is a way to clean up your workspace by bundling many wires into one. Instead of having 10 different lines for your models, prompts, and latents, you can plug them all into Oxidine and run a single wire across your workflow. It's smart enough to know which data is which, so when you plug it into a KSampler, it automatically sends the right info to the right place.
H4_Oxidine.usage: Plug your Model, CLIP, VAE, and Prompts into Oxidine. Take the single output and connect it to your other nodes. It will automatically provide the correct data types to whatever you connect it to.

source_1 / source_n.description:
Connect anything here. Additional slots appear automatically as you connect more inputs. Each slot accepts any ComfyUI type. 

 **CRITICAL SOCKET ORDER**: 
 - **Socket 1**: Usually reserved for your **POSITIVE** conditioning. 
 - **Socket 2**: Usually reserved for your **NEGATIVE** conditioning. 
 The proxy logic uses this order to ensure KSamplers don't get confused.

outputs.output: A single Sovereign Proxy object that internally carries all your connected data. When a downstream node queries it for a specific type (e.g., MODEL, VAE, CLIP), the proxy delivers the correct payload automatically.

features.name: Sovereign Proxy Protocol
features.description: Oxidine doesn't just 'pass' data; it becomes a chameleon. It mimics the behavior of whatever the receiving node expects. It implements dictionary, sequence, and attribute protocols simultaneously via Python magic methods (__getattr__, __getitem__, __iter__).

features.name: Deterministic Attribute Routing
features.description: If a node calls `.decode()`, it routes to the VAE. If it calls `.tokenize()`, it goes to CLIP. If it asks for `['samples']`, it goes to the Latent. It's surgical and safe.

features.name: Type-Aware Auto-Detection
features.description: Oxidine inspects every connected input and catalogs it by type—MODEL, VAE, CLIP, CONDITIONING, LATENT, IMAGE, MASK. No manual labeling required.

features.name: Zero-Copy Routing
features.description: Data is passed by reference, not copied. This means zero VRAM overhead for routing multiple types through a single cable.

features.name: Geometric Transmorphing
features.description: Change the node shape to Triangle, Hexagon, Octagon, or Circle via the context menu. No widgets required.

features.name: Stealth Wires
features.description: In Stealth Mode, wires become 95% invisible until you hover your mouse near them. Keeps the workspace industrial and clean.

features.name: Mood Shifts
features.description: The secret h4 shape can shift from (b'.')b to t('.'t) depending on your... mood.

tips: Be respectful of Oxidine. It's sensitive. If you feel 'cursed' while using it, check your socket order!
Socket 1 = Positive, Socket 2 = Negative. Always.
You don't need a context unpacker for Oxidine. Just plug the output directly into a KSampler's 'positive' and 'negative' slots—it will handle it.
For the deep architectural breakdown, see OXIDINE-BREAKDOWN.md in the root directory.

H4_DoubleSampler.title: H4 Double Sampler (The Two-Pass Engine)
H4_DoubleSampler.description: This is a versatile sampler that handles two stages of generation in one place. You can use it to create a base image and then immediately refine it to add more detail. It also includes an optional 'Chaos' mode that can add random variations to your prompts, helping you find interesting styles you might not have thought of.
H4_DoubleSampler.usage: Use this as your main generation node. Connect your models and prompts. If you want to try some random variations, click the button to open the Chaos drawer.

cfg.description: Guidance scale. 7.0-9.0 is the sweet spot.

denoise.description: Transformation strength. 1.0 is a fresh start.

enable_stage_2.description: Master toggle for the Refiner / 2nd Pass pass.

chaos_mode.description: (CHAOS DRAWER) Pick the injection style: Pure Chaos, Odds/Evens, Every #, or Random Pulse.

chaos_batch.description: (CHAOS DRAWER) Number of unique variants to generate in one run.

show_legend.description: (CHAOS DRAWER) Burn diagnostic stats directly onto the preview pixels.

outputs.IMAGE: Decoded preview image (with optional Legend burn-in).
outputs.SEED_OUT / CFG_OUT / etc: High-fidelity diagnostic outputs (Only visible when Chaos is ON).

features.name: Chaos Engine Subsystem
features.description: A sliding drawer UI that houses advanced entropy injection tools. It hammer prompt tokens with random weights in real-time, allowing for rapid style exploration.

features.name: Diagnostic Legend Burn-In
features.description: Professional-grade HUD. It burns Seed, CFG, Sampler, and Pass 1/2 stats into the top corner of your images so you never lose your settings again.

features.name: Dynamic Shuttles
features.description: Output pins that only appear when you need them. They export the internal 'truth' of the sampler for downstream logic processing.

tips: Keep 'Chaos Mode' on 'Random Pulse' for the most organic prompt discoveries.
Use 'Show Legend' when sharing images with friends so they know exactly how to recreate your masterpiece.
The Chaos Drawer stays closed by default to keep your workflow clean and professional.

H4_Switcheroo.title: H4 Switcheroo (Find & Replace)
H4_Switcheroo.description: A simple tool for swapping words in your prompt. You can replace one word with another across your whole prompt without having to find every instance manually. It's helpful if you want to quickly switch a character or an object in your scene.
H4_Switcheroo.usage: Connect your text prompt and tell the node what to find and what to replace it with. You can do up to 10 swaps at once.

subject.description: The thing you want to modify. This is your raw text prompt, a JSON string, or any text-like data. IMPORTANT: If you're working with prompts, wire the STRING output from your text node here, NOT the CONDITIONING output from CLIPTextEncode. Switcheroo needs readable text to find words in—CONDITIONING is just math.

swap_count.description: How many find/replace operations you want active. Set this to 2 if you have two pairs, 5 if you have five, etc. Slots beyond this number are ignored even if they have text in them.

clip.description: Connect your CLIP model here if you want Switcheroo to automatically re-encode your modified prompt back into CONDITIONING. This means you can plug the 'conditioning' output directly into your sampler without needing a separate CLIPTextEncode node. Leave empty if you just want the raw text output.

case_sensitive.description: OFF (default): 'Cat', 'cat', and 'CAT' are all treated the same and will all be replaced. ON: Only exact case matches get swapped. Use ON if you need surgical precision, like replacing 'Rose' (a name) without touching 'rose' (a flower).

find_1 through find_10.description: The word or phrase you're hunting for. This is what gets removed from your prompt. Leave empty to skip this slot.

replace_1 through replace_10.description: What replaces the found text. This is what gets inserted in its place. Supports multiline text for complex replacements.

outputs.data: The modified subject in its original format. If you passed a string, you get a string back. If you passed JSON, you get JSON back.
outputs.string: The final modified text as a plain string. Always available regardless of input type. This is what the Visual Terminal on the node displays.
outputs.conditioning: If you connected a CLIP model, this contains the re-encoded CONDITIONING tensor ready for your sampler. If no CLIP was connected, this is None.

features.name: Visual Terminal HUD
features.description: A live readout panel directly on the node that shows you the EXACT text being passed to your sampler after all swaps are applied. No more guessing whether your replacement worked.

features.name: Recursive Deep Crawler
features.description: If you accidentally wire CONDITIONING instead of text, Switcheroo won't silently fail anymore. It recursively scans the data structure for any embedded strings, and if it finds none (because CONDITIONING is pure math), it displays a clear error message telling you to rewire.

features.name: Wiring Fault Interceptor
features.description: Detects when you've wired raw Tensor data instead of text and prevents the CLIP encoder from trying to tokenize mathematical garbage. This stops the node from generating completely random unrelated images.

tips: ALWAYS wire the STRING (gray) output, not the CONDITIONING (orange) output, into the subject input.
If the Visual Terminal shows '0 matches', double-check your spelling and your case_sensitive toggle.
You can chain multiple Switcheroo nodes for complex multi-stage replacement workflows.
The 'conditioning' output is a convenience shortcut. It's identical to running CLIPTextEncode on the 'string' output yourself.

H4_ForgeMask.title: H4 Forge Mask (Canvas Editor)
H4_ForgeMask.description: An interactive tool for painting masks directly in ComfyUI. Instead of using a separate app, you can just paint the area you want to change (like a character's face or clothes) right on the node. It includes basic tools like a brush, eraser, and lasso to make the process easier.
H4_ForgeMask.usage: Connect an image and use the brush to paint over the area you want to mask. When you're done, click 'SEND MASK' to use it in your workflow.

image.description: The source image you want to mask. This is the canvas background. Connect it from any image source in your workflow.

mask_blur.description: The smoothness of the mask edges. A tiny bit of blur (4-8) helps the AI blend your changes without leaving hard, obvious lines around the painted area. Set to 0 for razor-sharp edges if you need pixel-perfect cutouts.

mask_strength.description: How 'opaque' the mask is. 1.0 means full strength—anything you painted gets fully processed. Lower it (e.g., 0.5) if you want your inpainting changes to be more subtle or semi-transparent, like a ghost overlay.

mask_expansion.description: Grows or shrinks the mask area after you paint it. Positive values (e.g., +8) expand the mask outward—great for ensuring the background blends perfectly around your cutout with no halos. Negative values shrink the mask inward for precision.

invert_mask.description: Swaps the selection. When OFF, the white areas you painted are what gets changed. When ON, everything EXCEPT the white areas gets changed. Perfect for 'protect this area and change everything else' workflows.

mask_data.description: The invisible code for your hand-painted mask. This stores the Base64-encoded PNG of your painting. The node manages this for you behind the scenes—you never need to touch it.

outputs.IMAGE: The original input image, passed through unchanged. It's a convenience passthrough so you can wire it directly to your inpainting sampler.
outputs.MASK: The processed mask tensor. White = change this area. Black = leave it alone. This goes into the 'mask' input of your KSampler or inpainting node.

features.name: Interactive Canvas
features.description: A full embedded painting surface rendered directly on the node. No popups, no external editors. Paint and see your mask overlay instantly.

features.name: Tool Rail (B/E/L/S)
features.description: Four tools in the left sidebar: Brush (B) paints mask areas, Eraser (E) removes mask areas, Lasso (L) creates polygon selections by clicking points (right-click or switch tools to seal), Shape (S) toggles between circle and square brush tips.

features.name: Dynamic Brush Slider
features.description: A vertical scrubber on the left rail. Click and drag to smoothly resize your brush from 2px to 512px. The live PX readout shows your current size.

features.name: Auto-Seal Lasso
features.description: If you have an active Lasso path and click 'SEND MASK' or switch to another tool, the path is automatically sealed and filled. No more lost selections.

features.name: One-Click Queue
features.description: The 'SEND MASK' button packages your mask data and immediately triggers a fresh generation queue. No manual queue button pressing required.

features.name: Upstream Auto-Sync
features.description: The canvas automatically detects when the upstream image changes (e.g., after a new generation) and refreshes the background without losing your mask.

tips: Use Mask Blur of 4-8 for natural-looking inpainting. Zero blur creates hard edges that look pasted on.
Use negative Mask Expansion (-4 to -8) to 'tighten' your mask when the AI bleeds changes outside your painted area.
Right-click while using the Lasso tool to quickly seal and fill your polygon selection.
The mask overlay appears as a semi-transparent white layer over your image—the brighter the overlay, the stronger the mask.

H4_CompleteLoader.title: H4 Complete Loader (All-In-One)
H4_CompleteLoader.description: The Universal Loader on steroids. It does everything the standard H4_UniversalLoader does—loads checkpoints, UNETs, CLIPs, VAEs, and LoRAs—but ALSO has built-in image upload slots. Up to 4 images can be loaded alongside your models, all from one node. Perfect for img2img, ControlNet, or reference image workflows where you'd normally need a separate image loader cluttering your canvas.
H4_CompleteLoader.usage: Set your load mode (Checkpoint or Component), select your models, and optionally upload images using the image_1 through image_4 slots. All outputs are available simultaneously.

load_mode.description: Choose between 'Checkpoint (Standard)' for .safetensors files or 'Component (UNET+CLIP)' for loading individual architecture components separately.

image_1 through image_4.description: Optional image upload slots. Select images from your ComfyUI input folder. These come out as individual IMAGE outputs alongside your model components.

outputs.MODEL / CLIP / VAE: Standard model components, identical to UniversalLoader.
outputs.IMAGE_1 through IMAGE_4: The uploaded images as proper ComfyUI IMAGE tensors, ready for any downstream node.

tips: This node inherits all the intelligence of UniversalLoader—GGUF detection, Wan/Z-Image heuristics, and Lumina/T5 dimension validation.
Use this instead of UniversalLoader + 4 separate LoadImage nodes to keep your workflow clean.

H4_MultiImgUpload.title: H4 Multi Image Upload (The Gallery)
H4_MultiImgUpload.description: A stripped-down batch image loader that dynamically reveals up to 10 image upload slots. Unlike the Complete Loader, this node ONLY handles images—no model loading. It's designed for workflows that need multiple reference images, style images, or batch inputs without any model-loading overhead. Each upload slot produces a paired IMAGE and MASK output.
H4_MultiImgUpload.usage: Start connecting or uploading images. New slots appear automatically as you fill them. Each image gets its own dedicated IMAGE and MASK output pair.

image_1 through image_10.description: Select an image from your ComfyUI input folder. Slots appear dynamically as you connect them—you'll never see more slots than you need.

outputs.IMAGE_1 through IMAGE_10: Individual IMAGE tensors for each uploaded image.
outputs.MASK_1 through MASK_10: Individual MASK tensors extracted from each image's alpha channel (if present). Solid white if no alpha.

tips: Perfect for H4_Mutate style transfer workflows where you need 4+ reference images.
Each slot is independent—you can upload different resolution images without issues.
The dynamic slot system means your node stays compact when you only need 2-3 images.
